news.title: UEFA to boycott World Cup if Infantino sell-off plan goes ahead
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. England, its fellow UEFA nations and CONCACAF have unanimously voted to boycott the upcoming men’s and women’s World Cups if Gianni Infantino goes ahead with plans to sell off shares in the tournament to private investors. UEFA’s 55 member nations held a virtual crisis meeting on Thursday to discuss Infantino’s recently announced plans to privatise and sell shares in the World Cup.

news.title: UEFA members unanimously boycott FIFA World Cup in protest over investment plans
news.lede: UEFA confirmed the meeting's outcome shortly after The Times reporter Martyn Ziegler, who also broke the news of FIFA's initial plans for the FIFA Forward Enterprise, reported it on Thursday afternoon. "UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors," UEFA's statement opened. news.title: Concacaf joins UEFA in solid front, unanimously rejecting FIFA World Cup stake sale
news.lede: 'The Confederation of North, Central American and Caribbean Association Football (Concacaf), meeting extraordinarily, decided unanimously to reject the proposal by FIFA and its president Gianni Infantino to sell the Football World Cup to private investors through the "FIFA Forward Enterprise" program.' "Concacaf and its 41 member associations have rejected the proposal. Concacaf reiterates that the future of football — and its main asset — must remain in the hands of the football family," reads the statement published by the organization. The 41 national federations belonging to Concacaf met this Thursday to deliberate on Infantino's proposal to create FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a subsidiary planning an initial capital raise of up to $4.2 billion, with a valuation of $20 billion, through long-term investors with minority stakes.

news.title: European nations vow FIFA World Cup boycott over Infantino private equity plan as opposition spreads
news.lede: GENEVA (AP) — European nations agreed Thursday to boycott the World Cup and all other FIFA competitions to protest Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell stakes in soccer’s biggest tournament to private equity investors. The North American soccer body rejected his plan later the same day. “UEFA and its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions,” the European soccer body said after an urgent online meeting of its 55 member nations. The next scheduled FIFA tournament is within weeks in Europe — the Women’s Under-20 World Cup hosted by Poland from Sept. 5 — and the four British federations comprise FIFA’s only bidder to host the 2035 Women’s World Cup.

news.title: Uefa agrees to boycott Fifa competitions if World Cup sell-off plans proceed
news.lede: Uefa agree stance at emergency meeting on Thursday. Boycott would begin with Under-20 Women’s World Cup. European countries have agreed to boycott all Fifa competitions if Gianni Infantino pushes forward with his proposals to sell chunks of the World Cup to US-based private investment. In an extraordinary development all 55 Uefa members resolved not to participate in future World Cups or other Fifa-run events, saying in a statement that they “unanimously and unequivocally reject” the proposals.
